issues.description: Email validation regex is overly simplistic and does not conform to RFC 5322. It will accept invalid emails like 'a@b.c' and reject valid emails with subdomains or special characters.
issues.suggestion: Use a more comprehensive email validation approach, such as a library like 'email-validator' or implement RFC 5322 compliant regex, or better yet, validate by sending a confirmation email.

issues.description: The ID generation using Date.now() and Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and may have collisions under concurrent load. This could lead to duplicate user IDs.
issues.suggestion: Use a secure random ID generator such as 'crypto.randomUUID()' or a library like 'uuid' or 'nanoid'.

issues.description: The email is converted to lowercase, but this is not documented in the JSDoc. Case normalization should be explicit in the API contract.
issues.suggestion: Add a note in the JSDoc comment explaining that emails are normalized to lowercase for consistency.

codeQuality.summary: Clean code with good practices including input validation, sanitization, and parameterized queries. Three issues identified: email regex validation is too simplistic (medium), ID generation lacks cryptographic security (medium), and email normalization is undocumented (low). Overall code quality is good but has room for improvement in security and validation robustness.

suggestions.description: Replace timestamp-based ID generation with Web Crypto API for better uniqueness and security
suggestions.benefits: Produces cryptographically secure, guaranteed-unique IDs (UUIDs) that are collision-resistant, more reliable than timestamp + random concatenation, and follows modern standards

suggestions.description: Consolidate multiple string replacements using a single regex or use a more maintainable approach
suggestions.after:
const escapeMap: Record<string, string> = { '<': '<', '>': '>', '"': '"', "'": ''' };
  return input.replace(/[<>"']/g, (char) => escapeMap[char]);
suggestions.benefits: Reduces repeated .replace() calls, improves readability with explicit mapping, easier to maintain and extend escape rules

suggestions.description: Validate and normalize email before sanitizing to ensure consistent data handling
suggestions.benefits: Ensures email is trimmed before normalization, prevents whitespace issues, provides defense-in-depth input handling
